claims: Section 4 of the 25th Amendment provides a constitutional mechanism for the Vice President and a majority of the Cabinet to declare the President incapacitated and unable to discharge their duties.
Section 4 of the 25th Amendment has never been used.
Upon such a declaration under Section 4 of the 25th Amendment, the Vice President immediately becomes Acting President.
Under Section 4 of the 25th Amendment, the Vice President and a majority of the principal officers of the executive departments (Cabinet) submit a written declaration to Congress.
Under Section 4 of the 25th Amendment, the Vice President immediately assumes the powers of the Presidency.
Under Section 4 of the 25th Amendment, the President can submit a written declaration to Congress stating no disability exists, allowing them to resume duties.
Under Section 4 of the 25th Amendment, if the Vice President and Cabinet dispute the President's return within four days, Congress must meet to decide the matter.
Under Section 4 of the 25th Amendment, keeping the Vice President as Acting President requires a two-thirds vote in both houses of Congress.
Section 4 of the 25th Amendment was created to address situations where a President is unable to function but cannot or will not transfer power voluntarily.
Sections 1-3 of the 25th Amendment address death, resignation, or voluntary transfer.
Section 4 of the 25th Amendment deals exclusively with involuntary transfer of power due to illness or incapacity.
In Section 4 of the 25th Amendment, "principal officers" generally refers to Cabinet members.
Whether "acting" secretaries can vote under Section 4 of the 25th Amendment is debated.
